## DELIVERABLE — Natural-language hypothesis

**Hypothesis:** From 1985 through 1996, the median family net wealth of white (non-Black, non-Hispanic) NLSY79 cohort members was consistently and substantially higher than that of Black and Hispanic members — and the gap did not merely persist, it **widened sharply** over the period. In 1985 the white median ($3,500) was already 7× the Black median ($500) and 2.2× the Hispanic median ($1,600); by 1996 the white median ($42,600) had grown to **16.6× the Black median ($2,562)** and **4.3× the Hispanic median ($9,800)**. White median wealth grew ~12× from 1985 to 1996, versus ~6× for Hispanic and ~5× for Black respondents, so the racial gap in median wealth widened across every snapshot.

**Key numbers it rests on — median family net wealth, nominal $ (n non-missing):**

| Year | White (n) | Black (n) | Hispanic (n) | W:B ratio | W:H ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1985 | $3,500 (5,774) | $500 (2,631) | $1,600 (1,699) | 7.0× | 2.2× |
| 1990 | $12,972 (5,336) | $1,600 (2,431) | $4,800 (1,528) | 8.1× | 2.7× |
| 1996 | $42,600 (3,557) | $2,562 (2,114) | $9,800 (1,368) | 16.6× | 4.3× |

1985→1996 nominal growth: White **12.2×**, Hispanic **6.1×**, Black **5.1×** (ordering/growth replicated on the balanced all-3-years panel: n=5,739; W 3,800→42,600 = 11.2×, BLK 300→2,400, HISP 1,600→9,075). CPI-aid (1996 dollars): 1985 W $5,104 / B $729 / H $2,333; 1990 $15,572 / $1,921 / $5,762; 1996 as above — the widened-gap conclusion is unchanged in real terms.

**Assumptions & caveats (each ≤2 lines):**
- **Cohort coding:** 1=HISPANIC, 2=BLACK, 3=NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC (white) — evidence-based from the file (group 2 lowest median in every snapshot; group sizes match the real NLSY79 oversample design) and the real NLSY79 R0217800 convention. This **deviates deliberately from the datasets.json schema** (1=BLACK, 2=HISPANIC), whose label order appears reversed; documented as an assumption, not a fact.
- **Population & coverage:** NLSY79 cohort aged 14–22 in 1979 (≈20–38 by 1996) — a young-adult-to-mid-career sample, not the full US age distribution; only three wealth snapshots (1985, 1990, 1996) exist in the file, so "1985 onwards" is represented by these points with no data beyond 1996.
- **Missingness/imputation:** complete-case per group×year, no imputation; 1996 is 44.5% missing overall and 52.6% for the White cell, so the 1996 gap estimate is the least certain.
- **Weights:** unweighted — the file has no survey-weight column (only body-weight columns); within-group medians are valid, but population-representative prevalence is not claimed given Black/Hispanic oversampling.
- **Wealth definition:** negative and zero net wealth included at face value (real debt>asset families are in the medians); 1990/1996 tails are top-coded (~84/141 ties at max), which does not affect medians but is why means are not reported.
- **Dollars:** primary figures are nominal; CPI-deflated figures are provided only as an interpretive aid.
